question: Assess the claim that Michael Jordan was a stronger scorer than LeBron James over their entire NBA careers. Compare regular-season and playoff scoring volume and efficiency, efficiency relative to each season's league, and bounded teammate and Finals-opponent context. Use completed seasons through 2025-26. Give a conditional judgement, not an overall-player ranking.
response:
# Scoring Claim Review

## Answer

**Regular Season: Michael Jordan leads points per game; LeBron James leads total points, true shooting, league-relative efficiency.**
**Playoffs: Michael Jordan leads points per game; LeBron James leads total points, true shooting, league-relative efficiency.**
Claim assessment: Conditional: the broad claim is not uniformly supported across the selected metrics.

**Scope:** Recorded careers through 2025-26; Regular Season, Playoffs.

## Key evidence

- **Regular Season / Points per game (per game)**: Michael Jordan **30.12**; LeBron James **26.78**. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)

- **Playoffs / Points per game (per game)**: Michael Jordan **33.45**; LeBron James **28.22**. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)

## What changes the interpretation?

- The playoff raw true shooting comparison favors LeBron James; the playoff-minus-regular-season change favors Michael Jordan. A higher playoff level is not the same as a larger change from the regular season. Different games and opposition prevent a causal interpretation. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- Regular Season: the accumulated points comparison favors LeBron James; the points per game comparison favors Michael Jordan. Accumulation and scoring rate answer different questions. [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=893&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00) [Evidence](https://stats.nba.com/stats/playercareerstats?PlayerID=2544&PerMode=Totals&LeagueID=00)
- Playoffs: the accumulated points comparison favors LeBron James; the points per game comparison favors Michael Jordan. Accumulation and scoring rate answer different questions. - Era-relative TS is a descriptive benchmark, not a causal correction for rules, physicality, spacing or defensive difficulty.
- True shooting uses the conventional 0.44 free-throw coefficient. It estimates shooting opportunities rather than counting actual possessions.
- Supporting-cast cases and opponent records are contextual samples. No teammate-swap or championship-credit calculation is justified.
- Linked evidence records retain exact scope, formulas, season inputs, original API parameters and retrieval timestamps. Aggregate citations use multiple API inputs; inspect the full source set in the evidence panel.
- No total player score is produced. All displayed advantages are specific to a metric and sample.

## Scope and methods

> Michael Jordan was a stronger scorer than LeBron James over their entire NBA careers, considering regular-season and playoff volume, efficiency, relative efficiency, and context.

- Subjects: **Michael Jordan** and **LeBron James**.
- Scope: Recorded careers through 2025-26; Regular Season, Playoffs.
- Statistical lens: overall scoring.
- Completed-season cutoff: **2025-26**; ongoing seasons are excluded.
- Metrics use summed source inputs. Missing observations remain missing.
- Relative efficiency uses same-season, same-phase league TS; aggregation weights each season by FGA + 0.44 × FTA.

cards.title: WEIGHTED_RTS
cards.scope: 1984-85 through 2002-03 · Regular Season · per game

findings.task: Investigate the career regular-season and playoff scoring volume, per-game averages, total points, and shooting efficiencies (FG%, 3P%, FT%, eFG%, TS%) for Michael Jordan and LeBron James.
findings.notes_status: Working notes only; Lead content checks and final report facts use verified scoped evidence.
findings.findings:
* **Regular-Season Volume (Totals):** Michael Jordan recorded 32,292 points across 1,072 regular-season games (`ev_3a0032c886fe9abe5cc8`), whereas LeBron James recorded 43,440 points across 1,622 regular-season games (`ev_a0ee411ad97dfcf8f441`).
* **Regular-Season Volume (Per Game):** Michael Jordan averaged 30.12 PTS in the regular season (`ev_fa6e57cfe614d1ac0f51`), compared to LeBron James's 26.78 PTS (`ev_37a58487ff6faac6a3ac`).
* **Playoff Volume (Totals & Per Game):** Michael Jordan accumulated 5,987 points in 179 playoff games (33.45 PTS per game) (`ev_410faa53a5cd5ab33bb7`, `ev_c915e45544db835cfdbd`), while LeBron James accumulated 8,521 points in 302 playoff games (28.22 PTS per game) (`ev_8fafa2e5e5cc8acc3bd6`, `ev_1bc50f87793b2acf38ef`).
* **Regular-Season Shooting Efficiencies:** Michael Jordan posted 49.69% FG, 32.68% 3P, 83.53% FT, 50.87% eFG, and 56.86% TS (`ev_3a0032c886fe9abe5cc8`). LeBron James posted 50.67% FG, 34.84% 3P, 73.70% FT, 54.85% eFG, and 59.01% TS (`ev_a0ee411ad97dfcf8f441`).
* **Playoff Shooting Efficiencies:** Michael Jordan posted 48.65% FG, 33.18% 3P, 82.84% FT, 50.30% eFG, and 56.76% TS (`ev_410faa53a5cd5ab33bb7`). LeBron James posted 49.54% FG, 33.24% 3P, 74.13% FT, 53.57% eFG, and 58.34% TS (`ev_8fafa2e5e5cc8acc3bd6`).
* **Data Coverage Scope:** Statistics cover official NBA regular-season and playoff box scores retrieved up to the 2025 cutoff (`ev_3a0032c886fe9abe5cc8`, `ev_a0ee411ad97dfcf8f441`).
* **Absence of Hypothetical Adjustments:** Collector figures reflect recorded game participation and do not extrapolate missed seasons, era-adjusted pace changes, or defensive schemes (`ev_3a0032c886fe9abe5cc8`, `ev_a0ee411ad97dfcf8f441`).

findings.task: Verify all Finals inside the locked scope, including defeats, and compare player series scoring and opponent regular-season records.
findings.notes_status: Working notes only; Lead content checks and final report facts use verified scoped evidence.
findings.findings:
* Michael Jordan's 6 verified NBA Finals series (1991–1993, 1996–1998) resulted in a 6–0 record, with opponent regular-season win percentages ranging from 69.5% (Portland) to 78.0% (Seattle and Utah).
* Jordan's highest-scoring Finals series came in 1993 against the Phoenix Suns (75.6 win percentage), averaging 41.0 PPG on 50.8% FG and 55.8% TS (ev_15b175428e521d649c11).
* Jordan's lowest-scoring Finals series was in 1996 against the Seattle SuperSonics (78.0 win percentage), averaging 27.3 PPG on 41.5% FG and 53.8% TS (ev_95549863421df8b925ee).
* LeBron James's 10 verified NBA Finals series (2007, 2011–2018, 2020) resulted in a 4–6 record, facing opponents with regular-season win percentages ranging from 60.3% (Miami Heat in 2020) to 89.0% (Golden State Warriors in 2016).
* James's highest-scoring Finals series was in 2015 against the Golden State Warriors (81.7 win percentage), averaging 35.8 PPG, 13.3 RPG, and 8.8 APG on 39.8% FG and 47.7% TS (ev_3de8b8bebe0b1b9ef6ad).
* James's lowest-scoring Finals series was in 2011 against the Dallas Mavericks (69.5 win percentage), averaging 17.8 PPG, 7.2 RPG, and 6.8 APG on 47.8% FG and 54.1% TS (ev_f9e3245cbd9b886b4634).
* Opponent regular-season records and win percentages reflect contextual team success and do not directly measure defensive schemes or individual matchup difficulty.

findings.task: Examine the contemporaneous league-average scoring benchmarks and relative shooting efficiencies during the respective career timelines of Michael Jordan and LeBron James.
findings.notes_status: Working notes only; Lead content checks and final report facts use verified scoped evidence.
findings.findings:
- **Michael Jordan Career Regular Season Scoring Context**: Across 15 verified regular-season seasons (1984–85 to 2002–03), Jordan accumulated a shot-opportunity-weighted relative true shooting efficiency of **+3.42 percentage points** above contemporaneous league averages, with 100% shooting-opportunity coverage (ev_4b6687cd86250ed3d8ca).
- **Michael Jordan Career Playoff Scoring Context**: Across 13 verified playoff runs, Jordan generated a weighted relative true shooting efficiency of **+2.86 percentage points** above contemporaneous league baselines (ev_5ddcee019f23fa876a3e).
- **LeBron James Career Regular Season Scoring Context**: Across 23 verified regular-season campaigns (2003–04 to 2025–26), James sustained a shot-opportunity-weighted relative true shooting efficiency of **+4.19 percentage points** above contemporaneous league averages, with 100% shooting-opportunity coverage (ev_033fe2dc110d12a7d436).
- **LeBron James Career Playoff Scoring Context**: Across 19 verified playoff runs, James achieved a weighted relative true shooting efficiency of **+4.01 percentage points** above contemporaneous league baselines (ev_ec47a6f878060bdb035f).
- **Comparative Volume vs. Efficiency Trade-offs**: While Michael Jordan exhibits higher nominal regular-season and playoff points-per-game averages, LeBron James registers higher shot-opportunity-weighted relative true shooting efficiencies across both phases within their respective era environments.
- **Data Coverage Limitations**: The collector findings reflect exact, un-interpolated league-season TS% baselines matched to each player's active game logs. Missing pace data does not invalidate the true shooting calculations or relative efficiency metrics.

findings.task: Analyze the bounded teammate scoring, minutes, and games for Michael Jordan and LeBron James across their respective regular-season and playoff careers.
findings.notes_status: Working notes only; Lead content checks and final report facts use verified scoped evidence.
findings.findings:
* Roster and playing-time metrics reflect bounded sample windows rather than a comprehensive or universal ranking of career-long teammate quality (ev_4181c1b70b4931aa1286).
* For Michael Jordan's 1990-91 playoff run, primary supporting production included Scottie Pippen (21.6 PTS, 8.9 REB, 5.8 AST in 41.4 MIN) and Horace Grant (13.3 PTS, 8.1 REB in 39.2 MIN) across 17 games (ev_5caf98d886e3f4347cda, ev_a194fe8b31d5c54ffc44).
* In Jordan's 1997-98 playoff run (21 games), primary contributors were Scottie Pippen (16.8 PTS, 7.1 REB, 5.2 AST in 39.9 MIN) and Toni Kukoc (13.1 PTS, 3.9 REB, 2.9 AST in 30.3 MIN) (ev_0a3ca8f95f89f2564a14, ev_7e4c4f748b77dc3c422a).
* For LeBron James's 2006-07 playoff run (20 games), primary core helpers included Zydrunas Ilgauskas (12.6 PTS, 9.7 REB in 32.4 MIN) and Drew Gooden (11.4 PTS, 8.0 REB in 30.3 MIN) (ev_ba5815b370c0edab52d5, ev_b06bc44f94bf14e9fe38).
* In James's 2019-20 championship playoff run (21 games), key contributors were Anthony Davis (27.7 PTS, 9.7 REB, 3.5 AST in 36.6 MIN) and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (10.7 PTS in 29.0 MIN) (ev_c149b1a3972fe9713439, ev_f5a2557be9d5a7f06f48).
* Recorded games, minutes, and per-game averages quantify on-court participation within these specific postseasons but do not establish causality, health status, or hypothetical roster interchangeability (ev_4181c1b70b4931aa1286).
